note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is. Each record is one line of one party page, matched to one race and one candidate on the lists already loaded in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (office, place and name all fit, one fit only). Colorado's November 3, 2026 ballot carries eight parties for state offices (Democratic, Republican, Libertarian, American Constitution, Approval Voting, Center, Forward, Unity); 'Unaffiliated' is not a party. Of Colorado's local contests only the retention votes for judges and the Regional Transportation District's directors are loaded; county, city and town contests are not, so a line about one of them is unmatched with that reason. Under 'endorsements' is only what a page itself calls an endorsement: the Broomfield County Republican Central Committee's Red Book ('BCRC Endorsed'; the committee's bylaws kept it neutral until the June 30 primary, and the page says it now endorses the Republican nominee in each race); the Denver Republican Party's '2026 Endorsed Candidates' (its home page, which also gives a 'Denver GOP Endorsement' in the City Council at-large vacancy election, a contest not loaded); the Clear Creek County Democrats' voter guide of 'Democratic Candidates on the November Ballot', which the party's own post 'Midterm Elections, November 3, 2026' says is where it has 'compiled their endorsements'; and the Forward Party's national list of 'our Forward endorsed candidates', which names Celeste Landry for Secretary of State. Every endorsement found is of a party's own nominee for an office the ballot prints with a party label; no party page read endorses a candidate in a nonpartisan race that is loaded. Under 'other_support', with the page's own words in 'kind' and never to be shown as an endorsement: the Libertarian Party of Colorado's 'Candidates 2026' (its nominees, chosen at its April 18 convention; the page does not use the word endorsed); the Colorado Republican Party's 'Candidates' page; the Colorado Democratic Party's 2026 Challengers class (campaign training and support for 18 legislative candidates in Republican-held districts); the Douglas County Republican Party's voter guide, which lists the party's nominees and municipal candidates and recommends 'Retain' for eleven judges; the Boulder County Democratic Party's voter guide, which lists the party's nominees and says of RTD District O 'Nonpartisan race. 2 Democrats running. Pick one.' (Audrey DeBarros and Jack Rosenthal); the Colorado Center Party's list of its candidates; and the national Constitution Party's 'Meet the Candidates' entry for its Colorado affiliate, the American Constitution Party. A line on a partisan office in such a list adds nothing to the party label on the ballot and is kept only so that each list is whole. Under 'recommended_against', a key of this file only: the Douglas County Republican Party's 'Do Not Retain' for Justice William W. Hood III and Judge Victoria E. Klingensmith. It is a party's published position on a nonpartisan retention vote but not support, so it is kept apart, and nothing in it is to be shown until John decides whether a party's 'do not retain' belongs on a judge's card. The Lieutenant Governor lines (Libertarian Wayne Harlos, American Constitution James Treibert) are unmatched because the official list names each ticket by its candidate for Governor. Lines matched although the page spells the name differently from the ballot keep the page's spelling in 'as_listed' (Michael Allen for Michael J. Allen, Fred for Frederick Espinoza, Thomas for Tom Cowhick, Jeff Livingston for Jeff K. Livingston, Desarai 'Dez' Packard for Dez Packard, Kathryn Green for Kathryn Kester Green, Mo Dower for Maureen (Mo) Dower, William Moses III for William Delano Moses III, Kevin L. Gulbranson, John C. Hjersman and John H. Sutton with or without the stop, Amanda Gonzales for Amanda Gonzalez, Stephen Hamilton for Stephen T. Hamilton, Timothy for Tim Martin, and judges with a middle initial the list leaves out). Two of the Democratic Challengers are not on the November list for their seats (Alec Lindeman, House District 58; Duane Gurule, Senate District 35): those lines are unmatched with the reason. Federal offices on these pages are outside this file, as are positions on ballot measures. Read on 2026-10-02 with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt checked first; every page in 'lists' was opened a second time and a record is kept only if the page still showed the name. Facebook pages, which are all some county units have, are social media and were not read. County units' pages that only list the party's own nominees for partisan offices, with no word of endorsement and no nonpartisan race, were read but not transcribed; they are named in 'not_read'.
